chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan, from Amr ibn Saeed, from Musaddaq ibn Sadaqa, from Ammar ibn Musa, who said:
I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the fermented drink, so he said to me: 'It is wine'.

key_terms.الْفُقَّاعِ: A specific type of fermented drink, often made from grains or fruits, mentioned in this hadith.
key_terms.خَمْرٌ: Wine or an intoxicating drink, the primary category for prohibited beverages in Islamic law.

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on fermented drinks like fuqqa' in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this concise narration from *Al-Kafi*, Ammar ibn Musa queries Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) regarding 'al-fuqqa'', a specific fermented beverage known in pre-Islamic and early Islamic contexts. The Imam’s definitive ruling that it is 'khamr' (wine) underscores the Shia jurisprudential principle that any drink causing intoxication, regardless of its specific name or preparation method, falls under the category of prohibited intoxicants. This classification reinforces the broader Quranic prohibition of intoxicants as 'defilement from the work of Satan'.
